issues.body: `newest_concluded_run` now skips every run whose conclusion is `cancelled`, but the motivating evidence only establishes that a concurrency-cancelled run with zero jobs may be non-adjudicating. A workflow can also be cancelled after one or more jobs have started. Such a run is positive evidence that the workflow was ingested, yet this code looks through it and can select an older `action_required`/zero-job run, causing M4 to report a stale rejection. The current tests pin only zero-job-shaped cancelled fixtures (and do not pass job information into this selection function), so they cannot catch this false-alarm path.
issues.fix_hint: Do not classify `cancelled` from conclusion alone. Preserve enough run/job evidence to distinguish a pre-job concurrency cancellation from a cancelled run that created or ran jobs, and treat the latter as an ingestion verdict. Add an anti-vacuity test with a newer cancelled run that has jobs over an older `action_required` run and assert that M4 does not resurrect the older rejection.
issues.title: All cancelled runs are discarded even when they executed jobs

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The self-lane observation is narrowly bound to the watched repository, workflow, and scheduled event, and the new tests exercise its pure, state-file, and live wiring. However, the new global treatment of every `cancelled` run as a non-verdict is broader than the evidence supports and can make M4 publish an older rejection after a newer run demonstrably executed jobs. Because that creates a false ingestion alarm and the suite does not cover the distinguishing case, this round requires changes.
